threat: Someone has armed the mine crews. The abbey thinks you are a mercenary; I think you fell out of a war that has not happened yet.
stakes: Keep the mine approaches open while we evacuate the novices.

threat: The forest patrols are disappearing between farms. Your rifle is strange, soldier, but the ambushes are familiar.
stakes: Reopen the civilian routes before the next supply wagon leaves.

threat: Hungry people make easy recruits for the Brotherhood. We need a corridor for food, not another speech from Stormwind.
stakes: Break the roadblocks without turning the farms into a battlefield.

threat: Lakeshire has no reserves left. You talk about fire teams and overwatch; teach us what those words buy against an army.
stakes: Keep the approaches to Lakeshire under friendly control.

threat: Your old war ended when the shooting stopped. Ours gets back up. Do not mistake a quiet road for a safe one.
stakes: Give the night watch enough breathing room to recover the missing.

threat: The engineers want to dismantle your weapon. I would rather watch it work. The pass needs clearing before the snow closes in.
stakes: Keep the mountain supply line from freezing shut.

threat: A breached dam would kill more people than any rifle. Find the pressure points in the enemy patrols and buy our surveyors time.
stakes: Protect the workers inspecting the approaches to the dam.

threat: Everything sinks here: carts, boots, whole patrols. The last convoy never reached the harbor.
stakes: Restore a route the next convoy can actually survive.

threat: You are not one of ours, but neither are the raiders. Bring discipline to this fight and you will earn a place at the fire.
stakes: Push the raiders away from the settlement routes.

threat: A rifle does not shorten these roads. The caravans need more than firepower: they need someone who understands an ambush.
stakes: Open a safe lane between the scattered outposts.

threat: Your weapon sounds like a storm, outsider. Use it carefully. The people gathering food on these trails cannot fight their way home.
stakes: Clear the threats around the gathering trails.

threat: The dead remember many wars, but not yours. Your arrival has upset several plans. Let us upset a few more.
stakes: Disrupt the hostile patrols before they discover our couriers.

threat: Messages keep arriving without their messengers. If your army trained you to move under fire, this is where we need it.
stakes: Break the hunting parties controlling the forest roads.

threat: The forest does not know the sound of your rifle. Neither do its invaders. We will see whether that unfamiliarity can protect our people.
stakes: Give the sentinels time to investigate the spreading corruption.

threat: The coast swallows both wrecks and rumors. Survivors have reported organized attacks inland, not wandering predators.
stakes: Keep a path open from the stranded settlements to the coast.

threat: Every faction calls this forest theirs. The refugees just want to cross it alive. You know what a contested corridor looks like.
stakes: Strip the hostile patrols of control over the crossing routes.

threat: The passes are being bought with blood. Your stories of soldiers watching each other's flanks sound useful here.
stakes: Prevent the mountain patrols from isolating the camps.

threat: There is no victory here without water. The strongest warband does not always win; the last one with supplies does.
stakes: Keep hostile forces away from the routes between the wells.

threat: These fields are worked by people, not flags. You have seen enough wars to know what happens when armies forget that.
stakes: Reduce the patrol pressure around the working farms.

threat: Every ruin has a claimant and every claimant has a raiding party. We need a position that can be held, not another banner.
stakes: Push hostile patrols back from the supply approaches.

threat: The jungle conceals whole armies. Your weapon will not help if you never see the shooter. Start by dismantling the patrol network.
stakes: Keep the expedition trails from becoming killing grounds.

threat: Smoke signals disappear in this fog. Our scouts do too. You claim your army could fight without seeing the whole battlefield.
stakes: Restore contact between the isolated marsh posts.

threat: Ancient ruins are poor cover when the enemy knows every doorway. We need fresh eyes, not another argument about ownership.
stakes: Open room for the expeditions to pull their wounded out.

threat: The desert kills the unprepared before the enemy gets a chance. We have lost water trains to armed raiders and cannot lose another.
stakes: Reduce the raiding pressure on the recovery routes.

threat: Our lookouts can see the whole valley but cannot reach the stranded patrols. Clear the approaches and we can bring them home.
stakes: Reconnect the ridge outposts before supplies run out.

threat: Old wars leave useful wreckage and dangerous owners. This salvage run is feeding a hospital, not an army.
stakes: Break the hostile screen around the salvage routes.

threat: The gorge is a furnace with firing lanes. Your army must have taught you something about crossing exposed ground.
stakes: Keep the extraction teams from being boxed into the gorge.

threat: The enemy can replace its losses. We cannot. Precision matters more than bravado on this front.
stakes: Disrupt the patrols holding our recovery teams back.

threat: You can shoot a body. You cannot shoot corruption out of the soil. Give our healers a perimeter while they do the harder work.
stakes: Hold the approach routes against the corrupted patrols.

threat: The instruments fail here and the wildlife eats the replacements. We need the expedition scattered back into one living group.
stakes: Clear room for the survey teams to regroup.

threat: The cold turns a small delay into a death sentence. Help us clear the patrol routes before the next storm seals them.
stakes: Keep the winter supply chain moving.

threat: Your old command cannot reach this battlefield. Ours can barely hold it. A soldier who still believes civilians are worth saving will do.
stakes: Give the relief columns space to recover the living.

threat: There is no rear line here, only places the dead have not reached yet. Make those places last a little longer.
stakes: Disrupt the enemy screen around the remaining refuge routes.

threat: The ground itself is an enemy approach. Your tactics were made for human wars; adapt them before this one buries us.
stakes: Keep the expedition camps connected under increasing pressure.
